provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — inbound Office attachments with macros are inspectable at the mail gateway/sandbox; endpoint detection lands at the macro-execution stage rather than delivery
medium — outbound clicks to newly-seen cloud/look-alike URLs are detectable at proxy/mail-URL-rewrite, though attribution requires infrastructure context

high — Office applications (winword/excel/powerpnt) spawning script/dropper child processes and writing a DLL/EXE, and execution of double-extension .ppt.exe, are high-fidelity endpoint signals via process-lineage and image-load telemetry
medium — link-click to file-download followed by execution is reconstructable from proxy + endpoint telemetry, but the click itself blends with normal browsing

detection_candidates.technique_name: Office Application Startup: Office Template Macros
detection_candidates.rationale: high — VBA macro execution that writes and launches a PE is detectable via Office macro-runtime (AMSI), VBA-project inspection and Office-spawns-child-process rules

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation/execution of wsc.vbs in %TEMP% via wscript/cscript and macro VBA activity are captured by script-block/AMSI and process-creation logging

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — a new Startup-folder shortcut named 'WinDefender' pointing to %TEMP%\NTSuser.exe (and the 'woolger' mutex) are actor-specific, high-fidelity persistence detections via file/registry and process telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Shortcut Modification
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation of a Startup .lnk whose target resides in %TEMP% is a rare, high-fidelity signal via file-creation and shortcut-target auditing

high — creation/growth of %TEMP% log files named wlg.dat / AdobeARM.log / AdobeARMM.log by a non-Adobe process, plus SetWindowsHookExW keyboard hooks from an unsigned %TEMP% binary, are strong host detections
medium — double-extension executables with document icons and PE files masquerading as .ppt are detectable via file-type/extension-mismatch and icon-resource heuristics, but need scanning coverage

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — names mimicking system/AV/Adobe artifacts (NTUSER.dat*.exe, NTSuser.exe, WinDefender, AdobeARM*.log, HousecallLauncher.exe) in %TEMP%/startup are detectable via name/path/signer baselining
medium — embedded high-entropy blobs/keys and encoded credential strings are detectable via static/entropy analysis, but require sample-level inspection
medium — growth of specific %TEMP% log files and their rename to a LOG_username_timestamp pattern before egress are detectable via file-write and file-rename telemetry
medium — local document collection is common; suspicious mainly in a backdoor/keylogger process-lineage and staging context
high — the distinctive /index.php?c=&r=&u=&t= URI pattern to hard-coded C2 IPs is a strong network-detection/IDS signature via proxy and TLS/HTTP metadata
medium — custom-encrypted C2 defeats content inspection but is detectable via the embedded key/algorithm in samples and via beacon-timing/destination analytics
medium — download of executables from cloud storage followed by execution, and appearance of companion binaries (wsnd.exe) alongside the keylogger, are detectable via proxy + file-creation telemetry

medium — the modified Core Impact agent and fake-HouseCall installer are detectable via sample signatures/hashes and their fixed C2 destinations, though a custom agent is less name-recognizable than commodity RMM
medium — outbound data to the fixed C2 IPs correlated with the GHOLE URI pattern is detectable at the network egress, but volume alone is subtle

detection_candidates.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
detection_candidates.rationale: high — outbound FTP from a workstation to the hard-coded exfil IPs, uploading LOG_username_timestamp files to a /woolen/ path, is a strong network-detection opportunity via flow/proxy logging and destination-IP blocklists

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — victim-side profiling and OSINT occur off-victim and are not endpoint-observable; intel/hunt candidate via targeted-user awareness and external exposure monitoring
low — organizational targeting research is off-victim; intel candidate only
low — actor-controlled social accounts are off-victim; brand/impersonation-monitoring and user-reporting candidate
low — attacker-controlled sender accounts are off-victim; inbound-mail sender/impersonation analytics apply at delivery time
low — compromise/impersonation of a third party's identity and mailbox is off the defender's network; intel/hunt candidate
low — adversary domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via newly-registered/look-alike-domain monitoring
low — off-victim staging on third-party services; intel/hunt candidate
low — payload staged on attacker-controlled cloud is off-victim until delivery; intel/hunt candidate
low — malware development is off-victim; the compiled artifact's runtime behavior is where detection lands — intel candidate
low — tool acquisition is off-endpoint; downstream deployment is where detection lands — intel candidate
low — third-party social-platform contact is off-victim and outside enterprise telemetry; user-awareness/hunt candidate
low — the harvesting page is off-victim adversary infrastructure; hunt candidate via mail-URL/proxy telemetry to look-alike login domains and impossible-travel logons after credential theft
low — credential capture occurs on attacker-hosted pages outside defender telemetry; hunt via post-theft anomalous-authentication analytics
low — self-deletion after in-memory load leaves little discrete signal; hunt via memory-resident/fileless detection and short-lived-file telemetry
